projects.title: Ecco the Dolphin: Defender of the Future Recompiled
projects.game: Ecco the Dolphin: Defender of the Future (Dreamcast version)
projects.status: The maintainer reports an end-to-end Linux playthrough including all levels, audio, and memory-card saves. Verified disc and host are Europe MK-5103350 and Linux x86-64; Windows and macOS are untested.
projects.summary: The Dreamcast SH-4 game code is statically recompiled to C++ ahead of time and runs with a native hardware runtime. The public repository contains no game code or data and requires the user's supported European disc image.
projects.strategy: Static SH-4-to-C++ recompilation with a native Dreamcast hardware runtime
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user-supplied Europe MK-5103350 disc image required; game data is not included
projects.subtype: Dreamcast static recompilation; Linux x86-64 target

projects.title: Phantom Hourglass Recomp
projects.game: The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass
projects.platform: Nintendo DS → Windows x64, Android ARM64
projects.status: The maintainer reports play on Windows 11 and a Pixel 8. On that phone, 3× rendering holds 60 fps while 6× can stutter as the device warms; other phones are untested. Only the supported USA dump and its listed D-pad patch are accepted.
projects.summary: The game's ARM9 program and 62 overlays are statically translated to C. The project uses melonDS for ARM7 and DS graphics/sound hardware, so the recompilation covers the main game CPU while a console core supplies the remaining hardware behavior.
projects.strategy: Static ARM9 recompilation with melonDS hardware core for ARM7, graphics, and sound
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user must supply a supported USA ROM; no game data is included
projects.subtype: Nintendo DS static code recompilation with Android application target

projects.title: Kirby & The Amazing Mirror Static Recompilation
projects.status: The experimental Windows build boots and runs more than 8,000 frames; the title, opening sequence, and first level render. Testing is concentrated in the first area, deep levels and bosses are unverified, and link-cable multiplayer is not implemented. Release v0.3.0 is marked prerelease.
projects.summary: The project statically translates the GBA ARM7TDMI ARM/Thumb instructions into C and models video, audio, DMA, timers, and interrupts in a host runtime. A built-in interpreter lets the game run while the compiled version is built; the repository and releases contain no ROM, BIOS, or game assets.
projects.strategy: Static ARM/Thumb-to-C recompilation with a first-run interpreter bootstrap
projects.source_available: Public source repository and prerelease; user must supply the supported USA ROM and BIOS; no game data is included
projects.subtype: GBA static recompilation; Windows x64 target

projects.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King Native Recompilation
projects.game: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King (GameCube version)
projects.platform: Nintendo GameCube → macOS on Apple Silicon
projects.status: The native macOS build reaches gameplay with working sound; logos, menus, the intro movie, and the Helm's Deep sequence are reported working. Only the opening levels are tested, and heavy fights run below full speed on the maintainer's M1 Max test system.
projects.summary: GameCube PowerPC code is statically recompiled to C with DolRecomp and compiled for Apple Silicon. Aurora renders the GameCube GX command stream through Metal, while a native host layer supplies console services; the project says no emulator runs during play.
projects.strategy: Static PowerPC-to-C recompilation with Aurora Metal rendering and native GameCube services
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user must supply the USA GameCube disc; no game data or generated code is included
projects.subtype: GameCube static recompilation for Apple Silicon macOS

projects.title: Muscle March Recomp
projects.platform: WiiWare → Windows, Linux, macOS, Steam Deck
projects.status: The beta README says the whole game is playable, while noting that the maintainer has tested few machines and controllers. It documents gamepad, keyboard/mouse, and Wii Remote plus Nunchuk input.
projects.summary: The Wii PowerPC game code is translated ahead of time into C++ and runs on a native host runtime for graphics, audio, storage, and Wii input. Users supply their own WiiWare WAD and Wii common key; the repository does not include game files.
projects.strategy: Static PowerPC-to-C++ recompilation with native Wii hardware services
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user-supplied WiiWare WAD and console common key required; game data is not included

projects.title: Project RE: Visited — Resident Evil 3: Nemesis
projects.status: The project publishes Windows releases, with v1.4.3 as the latest checked release. The README presents the native port and setup flow but does not state a full-campaign compatibility result.

projects.strategy: Clean-room static recompilation of PlayStation MIPS code to a native Windows executable

projects.title: Jet Moto 2 Recompiled
projects.status: Early Windows 11 x64 release. The README reports boot logos, menus, the attract demo, and one player-controlled race; sound, saves, other tracks, season modes, two-player play, and gamepads are untested.
projects.summary: The USA Championship Edition MIPS code is statically recompiled to C# with RecompOne into a native Windows program. The launcher rebuilds from the user's own disc; no game code or data is included.
projects.source_available: Public source repository and early release; user-supplied USA disc required; game code and data are not included

projects.title: Metropolismania PC Static Recompilation
projects.status: Very early experimental project. The native runner builds and reaches the Natsume logo, title screen, New Game, and the city scene with HUD, cursor, and 3D terrain; movies, sound, and saves remain in progress, and no playable game is claimed.
projects.summary: The USA PS2 MIPS R5900 executable is statically recompiled to C++ with PS2Recomp. The public source repository requires the user's own SLUS-20377 disc and does not contain game-derived files.
projects.strategy: Static MIPS R5900-to-C++ recompilation with a native PS2 runtime
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user-supplied USA SLUS-20377 disc required; no game files or generated code are included

projects.title: KOF '95 Static Recompilation
projects.platform: Neo Geo MVS/AES → Windows, Linux, macOS, PlayStation 5
projects.status: The README documents desktop builds and a native PS5 homebrew target, and claims locked 60 fps on PC and PS5. It does not specify a full-playthrough test boundary.
projects.summary: The project translates the Neo Geo Motorola 68000 program ahead of time into native C, with a native raster renderer and YM2610 sound synthesis. Building requires the user's own MVS or AES ROMs and Neo Geo BIOS; no copyrighted game files are included.
projects.strategy: Static 68000 recompilation to native C with a native Neo Geo renderer and sound path
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user-supplied MVS/AES ROMs and BIOS required; no game data included
projects.subtype: Neo Geo static recompilation with PS5 homebrew target

projects.title: Jet Set Radio Future PC Recompilation
projects.platform: Original Xbox → Windows 10/11; Steam Deck via Proton 11
projects.status: The README documents Windows 10/11 and Steam Deck use through Proton 11; Proton 11 is the only tested Deck runtime. Its Deck profiles are reported at a steady 60 fps. Only the North American retail release is accepted; the README does not state a full-campaign playthrough.
projects.summary: The original Xbox game code is statically translated to C and compiled into a Windows executable; the runtime supplies Xbox graphics, sound, controller, and memory-card services. Steam Deck is supported through Proton rather than a native Linux build.
projects.strategy: Static Xbox code-to-C recompilation with a native Windows runtime
projects.source_available: Public source repository; user-supplied NTSC North American Xbox game required; no game code or assets are included
projects.subtype: Original Xbox static recompilation; Steam Deck through Proton

projects.title: Chili Con Carnage PC Static Recompilation
projects.status: Windows 10/11 x64 beta v0.9.0 is available. The README documents a Direct3D 12 renderer and 60 fps in missions but does not state a full-campaign compatibility result; setup accepts only the USA ULUS-10216 image.
projects.summary: The PSP executable is statically recompiled to C++ with PSPRecomp and runs in a native Windows host for PSP firmware services, media, sound, controls, and saves. Game data is read from the user's own ISO and is not distributed.
projects.strategy: Static PSP executable-to-C++ recompilation with a native Windows host
projects.source_available: Public source repository and prerelease; user must supply USA ULUS-10216 ISO; no game data is included
projects.subtype: PSP static recompilation; Windows x64 target

projects.title: CallofRecomp: Call of Duty Classic for Android
projects.status: Pre-release v0.2.4. The maintainer says menus and components are under test and that a complete campaign has not been verified on physical Android devices; the current 60 fps Android target awaits another device measurement.
projects.summary: A game-specific static recompilation project for the PC 1.5 executable adapted to Android ARM64. The public repository and APK omit commercial files and require the user's compatible PC installation; Windows Subsystem for Android performance tests are tracked separately from physical-phone results.
projects.source_available: Public source repository and prerelease APK; user must provide compatible PC game files; no commercial assets are included
projects.subtype: PC game static recompilation with Android application target
